title: The real polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa inverse conjecture
statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}$ be a finite set. If $\xi\in\mathbb{R}$ is transcendental and $K_1,K_2\geqslant 2$ satisfy

$$
|A+A|\leqslant K_1|A|\quad\textrm{and}\quad |A+\xi A|\leqslant K_2|A|,
$$

then
**The real polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture.**

$$
(\log K_1)(\log K_2)\gg \log |A|.
$$

This conjectures the analogous estimate over the real numbers to the function-field result proved in the paper, asserting that simultaneous additive and multiplicative-translate structure forces the set to be small unless the doubling parameters are large. The source does not provide evidence that the real-number statement has been resolved.
source_name: Thomas F. Bloom, “A polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa inverse theorem for function fields”, arXiv:2501.11580 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.11580

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2025).
